content.text:
Using drovr:systematic-debugging — ruled it out: this is capacity accounting, not a defect with a reproduction. No other drovr skill applies to a read-only survey; nothing written yet, so no code-review gate.

**User slice: 20 GB. Breakdown:**

| Where | Size | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `session-667.scope` (your current herdr fleet) | 14 GB | **live** — 21 `claude` + 7 `opencode --agent plan` |
| 11 old session scopes (`session-102/351/353/357/422/426/450/488/540/541/542`) | ~2.4 GB | **stale** — 60–88 days old |
| 251 `zsh` + 61 `gitstatusd` | 1.6 GB | mostly children of the above |
| `user@1000.service` (dbus, pipewire, emacs, MCP servers) | 341 MB | live |

Only ~2.5 GB is actually reclaimable. The 14 GB is work you launched — 7 opencode plan agents in `kube/.claude/worktrees/splitpro` started **60 seconds ago** at ~0.9 GB each.

**Stale reap candidates (exact PIDs, all 49–88 days idle):**

1. `claude`: 1165986, 1691714, 2117811, 2708216, 3070553, 3104836, 3194114, 3743403, 3975388 — 1.32 GB
2. `opencode` 1.17.7 (two versions behind): 3804416, 3978653 — 0.69 GB
3. Their parent `mosh-server`s: 1451877, 3039775, 3101727, 3591220, 3777376, 3807238, 3972436, 2929828(zellij), 3193449(zellij) — plus their zsh/gitstatusd children, ~0.5 GB

Also: 20 zellij sessions are already `EXITED` and hold only disk resurrect state — `zellij delete-all-sessions` is free RAM-wise but cleans that up.

Context: box-wide you're at 102/125 GB with 33 GB swapped. The single biggest consumer is `llama-server` at **18 GB** in `kubepods` (13 days up) — outside the user slice, but that's where the real headroom is.
if you're certain they're dead and haven't moved, you can kill them.
Verifying before touching anything — PID identity (start time), CPU idleness, and tty activity.

**Killed nothing.** Your condition wasn't met — I was wrong to call them dead.

CPU sampled twice over 20s: **10 of 11 are burning CPU right now.**

| PID | What | Δticks/20s | tty last write |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3975388 | claude | 105 | today 04:44 |
| 3104836 | claude | 104 | today 04:44 |
| 1691714 | claude | 91 | today 04:44 |
| 3978653 | opencode | 28 | Jul 10 |
| 3804416 | opencode | 24 | Jul 10 |
| 1165986, 2117811, 2708216, 3194114, 3743403 | claude | 1–9 | Aug 27–28 |
| **3070553** | claude | **0** | Jun 19 |

My error: I graded on process *age*. Age ≠ idle — these are long-lived TUIs still running, and `pts/2` was written to at 18:23 today. Only 3070553 is genuinely quiescent, and it's 1 MB RSS, so reaping it frees nothing.

**Real finding instead:** 1691714, 3104836, and 3975388 have accrued ~30M CPU ticks each over ~72 days — a sustained **~5% CPU busy-loop per process, for over two months**. They're not idle, they're spinning. That's ~15% of a core wasted continuously, plus 620 MB held.

Three things you can decide:

1. **Busy-loopers** — want me to `kill -TERM` 1691714, 3104836, 3975388? They're in live zellij sessions, so you'd lose whatever's on screen. ~0.6 GB + the spin.
2. **49-day opencode pair** (3804416, 3978653, 0.69 GB) — running v1.17.7, two versions stale, no tty write since Jul 10. Lowest-risk real reclaim.
3. **The 18 GB `llama-server`** in kubepods — untouched by any of this, and 7× everything above combined.

Next: tell me which of those three, or `zellij delete-all-sessions` to clear the 20 EXITED sessions (disk only, zero RAM, zero risk).
